issues.text: old-rotation.ts is an orphaned file that serves a separate, unrelated purpose. It is explicitly legacy code ('Kept around in case we go back to the old rotation') implementing a different rotation scheme, not part of the flavor-of-day capability. This violates both 'No orphaned files' (nothing in the directory reaches it) and 'One capability per feature' (the directory contains two unrelated purposes).

The logic files do not follow the service conventions the spec incorporates: flavor.ts exports two free functions (todaysFlavor, announceFlavor) rather than a single run, returns plain strings instead of Results, and provides no consumer-grade failure handling (e.g., indexing into parlors with an empty list would throw rather than return an actionable error).

result.reason: The feature directory does not cohere as a single capability and violates the cohesion rules that are the core of the specification.

issues.text: Missing required entry point: The specification requires exactly one entry point 'index.ts' that re-exports the feature's entire public API, but no index.ts file exists in the feature directory.
Missing types file: The specification requires types to live in a dedicated '<feature>-types.ts' file, but no 'flavor-of-day-types.ts' file exists.
Orphaned files: Without an index.ts file, both 'flavor.ts' and 'old-rotation.ts' are orphaned files that cannot be reached through the import graph from an entry point.
File naming convention violation: The files 'flavor.ts' and 'old-rotation.ts' do not follow verb-first kebab-case naming (e.g., 'build-menu.ts', 'pick-winners.ts') as required by the specification.

Potential cohesion violation: The 'old-rotation.ts' file appears to serve a different purpose (old rotation system) than the main feature's capability (today's flavor), which may violate the 'one capability per feature' rule.

result.reason: The feature module 'flavor-of-day' violates multiple required criteria in the specification. It lacks the mandatory entry point and types file, has orphaned files, and doesn't follow naming conventions.
